sourceText: - **451. Short-term vs long-term** \[Slider\]: a clickbait change wins this week and loses users over months; surrogate metrics try to predict that.
title: Immediate clicks versus later value
lens: the horizon-specific incremental value assumption

sourceText: - **452. Bank run** \[Slider\]: set how many depositors fear a run and watch it become self-fulfilling.
title: A fear-driven toy withdrawal loop
lens: the amplification rule in a stipulated bank-run model

sourceText: - **453. Lucas critique** \[Gotcha\]: relationships in past data change once people react to a new policy.
title: A policy changes the fitted response
lens: the assumed coefficient after people react to a policy

sourceText: - **454. Braess's paradox** \[Gotcha\]: adding a road to a network can make everyone's commute slower.
title: A shortcut can raise equilibrium time
lens: selfish routing on the specified symmetric network

sourceText: - **455. Seasonal confounding** \[Slider\]: a campaign launched in December looks great because of Christmas.
title: A holiday changes both groups
lens: the seasonal comparison removed by a control trend

sourceText: - **456. Autocorrelation** \[Gotcha\]: treating correlated days as independent makes noise look highly significant.
title: Correlated days reduce effective draws
lens: the mean-variance ESS of a specified AR(1) series

sourceText: - **457. The drunk and her dog** \[Slider\]: two random walks that wander but stay tied together, cointegration in one picture.
title: Two wandering levels share a gap
lens: the common trend removed by differencing

sourceText: - **458. Time-varying confounding** \[Gotcha\]: today's treatment changes tomorrow's health, which guides tomorrow's treatment.
title: Treatment changes a later mediator
lens: the mediated path in a two-stage structural toy model

sourceText: - **459. Anticipation** \[Gotcha\]: people change behavior before a policy starts, contaminating the "before" period.
title: Anticipation contaminates the before
lens: the chosen pretreatment baseline in a contrast

sourceText: - **460. MusicLab** \[Story\]: in parallel worlds of the same song market, early download counts drove wildly different hits (Salganik, Dodds & Watts, 2006).
title: An early lead gets amplified
lens: the initial condition in a stipulated popularity recurrence

sourceText: - **461. PC algorithm, step by step** \[Slider\]: start fully connected, delete edges with independence tests, then orient colliders.
title: One conditional-independence step
lens: the isolated path test used as a discovery ingredient

sourceText: - **462. Which way is the arrow?** \[Predict\]: see a scatter and guess cause vs effect; noise that's even around the curve in one direction reveals it.
title: A direction must be stipulated here
lens: a structural direction rather than direction inferred from scatter

sourceText: - **463. Non-Gaussian clue** \[Slider\]: with non-normal noise, a linear model's direction becomes identifiable (LiNGAM).
title: A non-Gaussian noise clue
lens: the asymmetry of a specified noise distribution

sourceText: - **464. Cause–effect pairs** \[Measure\]: guess directions for real pairs like altitude and temperature; score yourself against algorithms.
title: A proposed direction needs a model
lens: observation versus intervention with a declared direction

sourceText: - **465. Poke the system** \[Slider\]: intervene on one variable at a time and watch the arrows lock into place.
title: Poke the variable rather than observe
lens: the incoming common-cause edge removed by an intervention

sourceText: - **466. Double machine learning** \[Slider\]: residualize treatment and outcome with ML, then regress residual on residual.
title: Regress residual on residual
lens: the residual projection ingredient of a causal estimator

sourceText: - **467. Naive ML bias** \[Gotcha\]: plugging a regularized ML model straight into a causal estimate biases it.
title: Regularization can shrink a slope
lens: the coefficient bias of a stipulated ridge fit

sourceText: - **468. Hidden confounder** \[Gotcha\]: discovery algorithms draw confident arrows that a missing variable fully explains.
title: A missing common cause explains a link
lens: the unobserved common-cause path in a toy graph

sourceText: - **469. Cancelling paths** \[Gotcha\]: a drug's direct and indirect effects cancel, so the data shows no dependence at all.
title: Direct and indirect paths cancel
lens: the total derivative when two structural paths oppose

sourceText: - **470. Invariance across environments** \[Slider\]: the true causes predict equally well in every hospital; spurious features don't.
title: A structural slope across contexts
lens: the invariant direct term versus context-dependent association

sourceText: - **471. Cows on beaches** \[Gotcha\]: a classifier fails on cows outside grassy fields because it learned the background.
title: A background shortcut meets a new mix
lens: the group composition behind a toy classifier accuracy

sourceText: - **472. The hospital tag** \[Story\]: a pneumonia model picked up which hospital took the X-ray rather than the lungs (Zech et al., 2018).
title: A hospital shortcut depends on mix
lens: the population mix of a stipulated shortcut classifier

sourceText: - **473. Domain shift** \[Slider\]: shift patient mix between hospitals and watch a predictive model's accuracy collapse.
title: Shift the population, keep group scores
lens: composition change with fixed group-level performance

sourceText: - **474. Counterfactual augmentation** \[Slider\]: flip a review's sentiment words but not its topic, and retrain to cut shortcuts.
title: Change a stipulated sentiment feature
lens: a fixed structural decoder rather than a retrained model

sourceText: - **475. Disentangling factors** \[Slider\]: slide one latent dimension at a time and watch a generated face change only in pose or light.
title: Two separately controlled toy factors
lens: the decoder's constructed separation of angle and light

sourceText: - **476. Ask a chatbot** \[Split\]: pose correlational and interventional versions of the same question and compare its answers.
title: Seeing and doing ask different things
lens: the declared structural model behind two differently worded queries

sourceText: - **477. Diagnosis network** \[Slider\]: toggle symptoms and test results; posterior probabilities of diseases update.
title: A symptom updates a supplied prior
lens: one diagnostic-network update with stated likelihoods

sourceText: - **478. Root cause in microservices** \[Slider\]: a latency spike spreads across services; trace it back along the causal graph.
title: A latency change travels along a path
lens: the direct and propagated terms of a toy service dependency

sourceText: - **479. Robust under intervention** \[Split\]: a causal and a predictive model face a policy change; only one keeps working.
title: A predictive slope under intervention
lens: the structural derivative after changing assignment

sourceText: - **480. Greedy score search** \[Slider\]: add, remove and flip arrows to improve a graph's fit score, step by step.
title: Score a candidate graph
lens: likelihood gain versus a parameter-count penalty

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **481. The Broad Street pump** \[Story\]: John Snow mapped 1854 cholera deaths around one London water pump.
title: A pump comparison needs denominators
lens: the descriptive rate contrast in an illustrative exposure table

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **482. Smoking and lung cancer** \[Story\]: Doll and Hill's 1950 study and their later British doctors cohort tied smoking to lung cancer.
title: An association and its common cause
lens: the observation-intervention gap in a stipulated risk-score model

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **483. Fisher's objection** \[Story\]: Fisher argued a gene might cause both smoking and cancer; Cornfield showed such a confounder would need implausible strength (1959).
title: How strong is a stipulated sensitivity?
lens: the specified risk-ratio sensitivity function

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **484. Hormone therapy reversal** \[Story\]: observational studies suggested heart protection; the 2002 Women's Health Initiative trial found harm.
title: A healthy-user story can reverse a sign
lens: confounding that opposes a stipulated intervention effect

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **485. Beta-carotene** \[Story\]: a 1994 Finnish trial found beta-carotene supplements *raised* lung cancer in smokers.
title: A treatment can increase toy risk
lens: the sign of an explicit absolute risk change

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **486. Semmelweis** \[Story\]: in 1847, handwashing with chlorinated lime cut deaths in his maternity clinic dramatically.
title: A clinic before-after rate contrast
lens: the denominator in an illustrative infection-count comparison

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **487. The Lanarkshire milk experiment** \[Story\]: teachers swapped frailer kids into the milk group, ruining a 1930 trial of 20,000 children (Student, 1931).
title: Frail children select into treatment
lens: baseline severity in a nonrandom treatment assignment

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **488. Tennessee STAR** \[Story\]: students randomly assigned to smaller classes in 1985–89 did better on tests.
title: A stipulated small-class effect
lens: the difference between two modeled educational outcomes

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **489. Sally Clark** \[Story\]: a "1 in 73 million" figure squared a single-death probability, assuming independence; her conviction was overturned in 2003.
title: Squaring requires an assumption
lens: the conditional probability needed for a joint rare event

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **490. Challenger** \[Story\]: plotting O-ring damage only for flights *with* damage hid the link to cold launch temperatures.
title: Leaving out the undamaged cases
lens: outcome-dependent selection in a damage sample

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **491. Google Flu Trends** \[Story\]: search-based flu estimates overshot the 2012–13 season by roughly double.
title: A probability forecast can overshoot
lens: the gap between a stated forecast and observed frequency

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **492. Dewey Defeats Truman** \[Story\]: quota-sampled polls in 1948 got the US election wrong.
title: A quota sample has a composition
lens: the group weights behind a toy electoral estimate

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **493. Moving to Opportunity** \[Story\]: children whose families won housing vouchers when young earned more as adults (Chetty, Hendren & Katz, 2016).
title: Age groups can have different effects
lens: the target population behind a heterogeneous intervention

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **494. The polio vaccine trial** \[Story\]: the 1954 Salk field trial involved about 1.8 million children, with a randomized placebo arm.
title: A randomized comparison still has counts
lens: the descriptive risk difference in a toy trial table

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **495. Scurvy** \[Story\]: in 1747 James Lind compared six treatments on sailors; citrus worked.
title: Compare two stipulated remedy groups
lens: the denominators of an illustrative treatment comparison

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **496. Hawthorne revisited** \[Story\]: reanalysis of the original factory lighting data found little support for the famous effect (Levitt & List, 2011).
title: A famous story meets later evidence
lens: the sensitivity to which study estimates are included

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **497. Streptomycin** \[Story\]: the 1948 UK Medical Research Council trial was among the first properly randomized clinical trials.
title: A trial contrast in standardized units
lens: the outcome spread behind a standardized estimate

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **498. The Netflix Prize** \[Story\]: teams blended hundreds of models to beat Netflix's recommender by 10%, winning $1 million in 2009.
title: A blended predictor under toy risks
lens: the stipulated variance reduction in an ensemble risk calculation

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **499. Observing Dark Worlds** \[Story\]: a 2012 Kaggle contest asked teams to locate invisible dark matter halos from distorted galaxy shapes; Bayesian MCMC models took the top two places.
title: One-axis halo-location update
lens: a normal measurement ingredient rather than full shear inference

sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
sourceText: - **500. A 29% chance happens** \[Story\]: forecasts giving Trump about a 29% chance in 2016 weren't "wrong" when he won; one-in-three events are common.
title: One outcome does not judge a forecast
lens: repeated calibration versus a single realized election

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **502. The hockey stick** \[Slider\]: plot average wait against utilization; going from 80% to 90% busy doubles the wait.
title: Near capacity, waiting grows sharply
lens: the load gap in a stable queueing model

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **504. Random vs fixed service** \[Split\]: same average service time; fixed times cut queue waits in half (M/M/1 vs M/D/1).
title: Fixed service removes one variance term
lens: service variability with the same average service time

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **505. Variability kills** \[Slider\]: keep the average service time, raise its variance, and watch the queue grow.
title: The same service mean, different tails
lens: the second moment of service in an M/G/1 mean wait

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **506. Add a second barista** \[Predict\]: waits fall by far more than half, often by over 90% at high load.
title: Add another pooled server
lens: the pooled-server waiting probability and delay

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **507. One fast or two slow?** \[Split\]: one server at double speed vs two normal servers; compare waits and total time.
title: One fast server or two slower ones
lens: waiting and total time at equal total service capacity

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **508. Merge the call centers** \[Slider\]: pool ten small centers into one and see the same service level with fewer agents.
title: Pooling removes isolated spare capacity
lens: the symmetric single-center versus pooled-center model

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **509. Bursty arrivals** \[Slider\]: same average arrival rate, but in bursts; the queue looks completely different.
title: Bursts raise the variability factor
lens: arrival variability in a stated queueing approximation

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **510. Balking and reneging** \[Slider\]: customers who see a long line leave, or give up after waiting; watch lost sales.
title: Some queued customers abandon the sale
lens: the retained-customer share in a supplied service funnel

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **511. Erlang C staffing** \[Slider\]: how many agents are needed to answer 80% of calls within 20 seconds?
title: A service threshold enters Erlang C
lens: the staffing input of an explicit queueing model

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **512. Square-root staffing** \[Slider\]: as call volume grows, the safety margin of extra agents grows only with its square root.
title: The reserve scales with a square root
lens: the stated staffing-rule safety margin

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **513. Warm-up period** \[Predict\]: an empty queue takes time to reach steady state; early measurements mislead.
title: A snapshot depends on its starting queue
lens: the transient starting state of a deterministic fluid queue

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **514. PASTA** \[Gotcha\]: random arrivals see the average queue; scheduled arrivals, like booked appointments, don't.
title: Long states get more time exposure
lens: time-weighted observation rather than a general PASTA proof

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **515. Restaurant tables** \[Slider\]: tune reservations vs walk-ins and see table turnover and waits.
title: A toy pooled-table capacity model
lens: steady Poisson arrivals rather than a reservation schedule

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **516. Skyscraper elevators** \[Slider\]: morning rush in a 40-floor building; zoning floors to elevators cuts waits.
title: Stops add overhead to an elevator round
lens: the deterministic timing facet of floor zoning

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **517. Virtual queue** \[Split\]: a theme-park ride with and without return-time tickets; same capacity, very different experience.
title: A virtual place moves the waiting
lens: in-line time without changing the stipulated total wait

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **518. Express lane threshold** \[Slider\]: set the item limit and watch both lanes' waits balance.
title: A shorter-job lane changes service mix
lens: the service distribution supplied to a toy express queue

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **519. ER at 95% capacity** \[Slider\]: push a hospital emergency department near full and watch boarding delays cascade.
title: Little slack near full capacity
lens: the nonlinear waiting-time effect near service capacity

sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
sourceText: - **520. Kingman's formula** \[Slider\]: wait ≈ variability × utilization × service time, with each factor on its own slider.
title: Variability, load and service duration
lens: the three factors in a stated heavy-traffic approximation

sourceText: - **522. Shortest queue vs random** \[Split\]: watch two server farms side by side, one routing randomly, one to the shortest line.
title: One arrival can choose the shorter line
lens: routing with observed equal-duration jobs

sourceText: - **523. Load balancer showdown** \[Slider\]: round robin vs least-connections under uneven job sizes.
title: Few jobs can mean much outstanding work
lens: job counts versus remaining workload

sourceText: - **525. FIFO, LIFO, sharing** \[Split\]: the same jobs under three scheduling rules; compare waits and fairness.
title: Which of two jobs goes first?
lens: the mean wait in two explicitly ordered jobs

sourceText: - **526. The tail at scale** \[Gotcha\]: fan a request out to 100 servers and one server's rare slowness becomes the typical user's experience (Dean & Barroso, 2013).
title: A fan-out inherits one slow component
lens: the union of independent slow-request events

sourceText: - **527. Hedged requests** \[Slider\]: send a backup request after a short delay and cut tail latency for a little extra load.
title: Independent backups must both be slow
lens: the joint slow-tail event in a two-copy toy model

sourceText: - **528. Factory network** \[Slider\]: jobs flow through linked stations; the busiest one sets everyone's pace.
title: A serial line has one limiting station
lens: the smallest supplied station capacity

sourceText: - **529. Find the bottleneck** \[Predict\]: guess which station limits a production line, then speed it up and watch the bottleneck move.
title: Speed up the binding station
lens: the movement of a deterministic capacity bottleneck

sourceText: - **530. WIP limits** \[Slider\]: cap work in progress on a kanban board and watch cycle time fall.
title: Less work at the same throughput
lens: compatible long-run WIP and throughput averages

sourceText: - **531. Retry storms** \[Slider\]: a brief slowdown triggers retries that keep the system overloaded long after the cause is gone.
title: Retries can exceed available capacity
lens: the stipulated effective arrival rate after retries

sourceText: - **532. Backpressure** \[Slider\]: let a slow service push back on callers and the pile-up stops spreading.
title: Backpressure caps the incoming rate
lens: the fluid input-capacity gap

sourceText: - **533. Autoscaling lag** \[Slider\]: new servers take minutes to start; a traffic spike outruns them.
title: Scaling lag gives a deficit time to grow
lens: the duration of a stipulated capacity shortfall

sourceText: - **534. Head-of-line blocking** \[Gotcha\]: one slow job at the front stalls fast jobs behind it.
title: The long front job delays a short job
lens: the two-job head-of-line waiting calculation

sourceText: - **535. Priority starvation** \[Slider\]: raise high-priority traffic and watch low-priority jobs never get served.
title: High priority consumes the spare service
lens: the residual capacity available to a low-priority fluid queue

sourceText: - **536. Traffic light timing** \[Slider\]: tune green times at an intersection and see queues on each road.
title: A green-time share sets average capacity
lens: the supplied signal duty cycle in a fluid model

sourceText: - **537. Airport security** \[Slider\]: open or close lanes as flights bunch up and see missed-flight risk.
title: An extra security lane changes the wait
lens: the server count in a stated steady queue

sourceText: - **538. Ride-hailing dispatch** \[Slider\]: drivers cycle between idle, en route and busy; demand spikes drain idle drivers.
title: Idle drivers are an inflow-outflow stock
lens: the assumed returns and request rates of an idle-driver buffer

sourceText: - **539. The bus loop** \[Slider\]: one server visiting several queues in turn; buses bunch together over time.
title: A fixed polling loop pays switch time
lens: the one-job-per-visit timing facet of a polling cycle

sourceText: - **540. Your team's queue** \[Measure\]: enter work in progress and throughput to compute your team's average cycle time with Little's law.
title: Turn team WIP into a cycle-time estimate
lens: the long-run system boundary required by Little's law

sourceText: - **542. Split and merge streams** \[Slider\]: thin one Poisson stream into two, or merge two into one; both stay Poisson.
title: Thin, then merge independent streams
lens: independent thinning and superposition rates

sourceText: - **543. Traffic by hour** \[Slider\]: draw a daily arrival-rate curve and watch visits pulse with it.
title: Integrate a changing hourly arrival rate
lens: the area under a stated linear intensity

sourceText: - **544. Aftershocks** \[Slider\]: a self-exciting Hawkes process where each event raises the chance of more, like earthquakes or retweets.
title: Events create expected descendants
lens: the subcritical offspring multiplier

sourceText: - **545. Replacing bulbs** \[Slider\]: a renewal process; tune lifetime spread and see replacement timing smooth out.
title: Renewal spread changes the residual wait
lens: the second-moment inspection effect at a fixed mean lifetime

sourceText: - **546. Insurance claims** \[Slider\]: random claim times with random sizes; total payout builds in jumps.
title: A random count of random claims
lens: claim-count and claim-size uncertainty

sourceText: - **548. Extinction threshold** \[Slider\]: average offspring below 1 always dies out; just above 1 often still dies.
title: Subcritical and supercritical lineages
lens: the eventual extinction fixed point

sourceText: - **549. Family tree** \[Predict\]: grow a random branching tree and guess whether it survives 20 generations.
title: Extinction by a finite generation
lens: the generating-function iterate before the eventual limit

sourceText: - **550. Mean reversion** \[Slider\]: an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck path wanders but keeps being pulled back to its mean.
title: An expected path returns toward its mean
lens: conditional mean reversion in a stipulated diffusion

sourceText: - **551. Stock price paths** \[Slider\]: geometric Brownian motion; raise volatility and the fan of paths widens.
title: Volatility separates mean and median
lens: the lognormal terminal distribution under specified parameters

sourceText: - **552. Lévy flight vs random walk** \[Split\]: a few huge jumps vs many small steps, the two styles of animal foraging.
title: Rare long jumps change a bounded mean
lens: a finite jump-mixture facet rather than a stable Levy process

sourceText: - **553. Random telegraph** \[Slider\]: a signal that flips between two states at random times.
title: A two-state signal forgets its start
lens: continuous-time transition rates in a two-state signal

sourceText: - **554. Immigration and death** \[Slider\]: a population fed by arrivals and drained by deaths settles into a Poisson-shaped balance.
title: Arrivals offset per-capita departures
lens: the mean balance of an immigration-death model

sourceText: - **555. Genetic drift** \[Slider\]: in a Moran model, a neutral gene randomly takes over or vanishes in a small population.
title: A neutral allele can take over
lens: the initial frequency under a neutral finite-population model

sourceText: - **556. Wright–Fisher** \[Slider\]: watch many allele-frequency paths drift to 0 or 1, faster in small populations.
title: Small populations drift more
lens: the conditional one-generation Wright-Fisher spread

sourceText: - **557. Clustered, random or regular?** \[Split\]: three tree maps; guess which is Poisson, which clustered, which repulsive.
title: Uniform placement still leaves gaps
lens: the empty-cell baseline of an independent spatial toy model

sourceText: - **558. Voronoi cells** \[Slider\]: drop random seed points and the plane splits into cells, like cracked mud or giraffe spots.
title: The boundary between two line seeds
lens: the one-dimensional equal-distance Voronoi boundary

sourceText: - **559. First passage** \[Slider\]: how long until a Brownian path first hits a barrier? The distribution has a heavy tail.
title: First hit within a finite horizon
lens: the absorbing finite-lattice analogue of first passage

sourceText: - **560. Brownian bridge** \[Slider\]: random paths pinned at both ends, the shape behind many statistical tests.
title: Pin both ends of a random path
lens: the Brownian-bridge variance profile

sourceText: - **563. How fast does it mix?** \[Slider\]: plot distance from uniform after each shuffle of a deck.
title: A chain approaches stationarity
lens: the exact two-state total-variation distance

sourceText: - **564. The cutoff** \[Gotcha\]: some chains stay far from mixed, then mix almost all at once.
title: A collection transition can be sharp
lens: the coupon-completion analogy rather than a general cutoff theorem

sourceText: - **565. Absorbing states** \[Predict\]: guess the expected steps until a board game ends, then compute it exactly.
title: Absorption time in a finite toy board
lens: the expected stopping time between two absorbing boundaries

sourceText: - **566. Hitting probabilities** \[Slider\]: from each square, the chance of reaching the goal before the trap, colored live.
title: The goal competes with a trap
lens: the fair-walk hitting probability between two boundaries

sourceText: - **567. Detailed balance** \[Slider\]: flows between each pair of states cancel, a property that MCMC relies on.
title: Forward and reverse stationary flow
lens: detailed balance in a specified two-state chain

sourceText: - **568. Periodic chains** \[Gotcha\]: a chain that alternates between two sets never settles, even though it has a stationary distribution.
title: A periodic chain keeps its oscillation
lens: a stationary law without convergence from a fixed start

sourceText: - **569. Spectral gap** \[Slider\]: the second eigenvalue sets the mixing speed; drag graph edges and watch it change.
title: The second eigenvalue changes the decay
lens: the spectral-gap facet of a two-state mixing model

sourceText: - **570. Barbell graph** \[Slider\]: two dense clusters joined by one edge mix very slowly.
title: A tiny cross-cluster transition is slow
lens: the coarse two-state bottleneck analogy

sourceText: - **571. Customer journeys** \[Slider\]: model site pages as states and watch visitors flow to purchase or exit.
title: A toy journey reaches a purchase stage
lens: the conditional probabilities in a finite conversion path

sourceText: - **572. Removal effect attribution** \[Slider\]: delete one channel from the journey chain and see how many conversions vanish.
title: A modeled channel-removal contrast
lens: the specified without-channel counterfactual

sourceText: - **573. Credit ratings** \[Slider\]: yearly transitions between AAA and default; project a bond's path decades out.
title: A constant annual default hazard
lens: the survival complement under a constant conditional hazard

sourceText: - **574. Markov melodies** \[Slider\]: generate music from note-transition probabilities, then raise the order.
title: A two-note Markov melody
lens: the next-state mixture in a stipulated note-transition model

sourceText: - **575. Coupling from the past** \[Slider\]: run chains from every start until they merge, giving an exact sample.
title: Independent chances for a coupling event
lens: a supplied coalescence-opportunity model rather than full CFTP

sourceText: - **576. Ising magnet** \[Slider\]: flip spins on a grid at a set temperature; below a critical point, big domains form.
title: One spin listens to its neighbors
lens: the conditional probability at one Ising site

sourceText: - **577. The Kruskal count** \[Gotcha\]: two people following card-count paths almost always land on the same card.
title: A toy pair of paths can meet
lens: the independent meeting-chance analogy to card-path coalescence

sourceText: - **578. Cover time** \[Predict\]: how long until a random walker visits every node of a graph?
title: Visit every node of a complete graph
lens: the collection stages of a uniform complete-graph walk

sourceText: - **579. Weather from umbrellas** \[Predict\]: infer hidden weather from whether a colleague carries an umbrella, with a hidden Markov model.
title: An umbrella updates predicted weather
lens: one measurement update using a supplied hidden-state prior

sourceText: - **580. Machine up and down** \[Slider\]: a continuous-time chain of breakdowns and repairs; set rates and see availability.
title: Repair and failure set availability
lens: the rates of a two-state continuous-time machine

sourceText: - **582. Step size** \[Slider\]: tiny steps crawl, huge steps get rejected; find the sweet spot by the acceptance meter.
title: A large proposal can be rejected
lens: the acceptance ratio under a symmetric standard-normal proposal

sourceText: - **584. Burn-in** \[Predict\]: start far away and guess when the chain has forgotten its starting point.
title: The starting state fades with steps
lens: the finite-time transient in a specified chain

sourceText: - **585. Four chains, one answer** \[Slider\]: start chains in different corners; R-hat drops toward 1 as they agree.
title: Within and between chains disagree
lens: the classic variance-ratio diagnostic under supplied summaries

sourceText: - **586. The banana** \[Slider\]: random-walk Metropolis struggles along a curved posterior while Hamiltonian Monte Carlo glides through it.
title: A curved target has a different energy
lens: the energy cross-section of a stipulated banana density

sourceText: - **587. Rolling marbles** \[Slider\]: HMC as a frictionless marble rolling across the negative log-density, with momentum.
title: A momentum step follows a potential
lens: the position and energy error of one harmonic leapfrog step

sourceText: - **588. The U-turn** \[Slider\]: NUTS stops a trajectory once it starts doubling back; watch the tree grow and halt.
title: A path begins moving back toward home
